Pre-Retrieval Process • Optimizing Data Indexing The aim of optimizing data indexing is to boost the quality of the content being indexed. At present, there are five primary strategies being used to achieve this: enhancing the granularity of indexed data, optimizing index structures, adding metadata, alignment optimization, and mixed retrieval.

evidence.text: Fine-tuning an Embedding model differs from the process used for a standard language model, primarily in terms of the datasets employed. In the prevalent approach to fine-tuning embedding models, the dataset consists of three main components: queries, corpus, and relevant docs. The embedding model searches for relevant documents in the corpus based on the query. Subsequently, the retrieval of relevant docs for the query, or lack thereof, serves as a metric for evaluating the model’s performance. During the construction of datasets, fine-tuning of models, and the evaluation process, various challenges may arise within each of these three components. 7 RAG Evaluation With the rapid development and increasing applications of RAG in the NLP field, evaluating the performance and effectiveness of RAG models has become a focal point of research in the LLMs community. The aim of evaluation is to help understand and optimize the performance of RAG models in various application scenarios. In a significant amount of past research, the evaluation of RAG models mainly focused on their performance in specific downstream tasks, using standard assessment metrics and methods tailored to these tasks. 7.3 Evaluation Framework: Benchmarks and Tools This section introduces the evaluation framework for RAG, including benchmark tests and automated evaluation tools. These tools and tests not only provide quantitative metrics for the performance of RAG models but also help to deepen the understanding of the model’s performance across various evaluation targets and aspects. The current state-of-the-art benchmark tests include RGB and RECALL[Chen et al., 2023b, Liu et al., 2023b], which are aimed at evaluating the required abilities of RAG models; while the latest automated evaluation tools include RAGAS[Es et al., 2023], ARES[Saad-Falcon et al., 2023], and TruLens. Limitations.summary: Overall, the technical stack of RAG’s toolchain has initially formed, and many enterprise-level applications have gradually emerged, but an all-in-one platform still needs to be refined.

evidence.text: I-native frameworks, traditional software or cloud service providers have also expanded their service range. For instance, Verba9, provided by the vector database company Weaviate, focuses on personal assistants. Amazon offers its users the intelligent enterprise search service tool Kendra, based on RAG thinking. Users can search in different content repositories through built-in connectors. The development of the technical stack and RAG are mutually reinforcing. New technologies pose higher demands on the existing technical stack, while the optimization of the technical stack’s functions further promotes the development of RAG technology.
